::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 10th 1885  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Gatty](people/person_469.qmd)

‘[A bit of Green](other_books/otherbook_987.qmd)’ was only in the number preceding ‘[the Blackbird’s Nest](other_books/otherbook_988.qmd)’- July 1861.[^1] I had been on the like quest for the sake of the few words I have said in a conversation on books in the August number, I should have done so in the July one only that it was another persons conversation into which [it] would not fit

I did not write to you for what can I say but how grieved I am, as if a bright light had been taken away, or more truly a lamp become a star, as in that poem of BM’s.

Almost every letter I get has some note of mourning for [one](people/person_494.qmd)who had become dear to so many

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Juliana Ewing had died on 13 May 1885.  Her sister Horatia was probably gathering material for her *Juliana Horatia Ewing and Her Books* (1885).  'A Bit of Green' and 'The Blackbird's Nest' had been Ewing's two earliest contributions to *MP*.  In 'A Conversation on Books' *MP* 3s 10 (August 1885) 62, Arachne discusses Ewing's career, expressing 'our grief that one to whom we all owe so much, should have been taken from us so early.'
